column1: # ================ *** THE THREE SOURCES OF NOISE, NAMED *** ================
# 1. *** THE NISSAN SERENA. *** Nineteen-nineties motor advertisements OCR the model name as "lERENA".
#    They are the single largest block of results and they swamp everything.
# 2. *** "GUTTA SERENA" *** - the old medical term for blindness of the optic nerve, common in
#    eighteenth and nineteenth century infirmary tables and medical columns. OCRs as "gutta lerena".
# 3. *** DON PEDRO LOPEZ DE LERENA *** - Spanish Minister of Finance under Charles III, reported in the
#    British press from the London Gazette in the 1780s and 90s as "Monf. de Lerena". A real Lerena, of
#    a real Spanish family, and NOT ours - and a trap for anyone searching the name cold.
# *** DO NOT SEARCH THIS FAMILY BY SURNAME IN THE BRITISH PRESS. *** It is the same lesson the Uruguayan
# registers taught - a family written eight ways is not reachable by its name - arriving from a
# completely different direction, and for a different reason: here the name is not mis-written, it is
# COLLIDED WITH.
# *** THE LIVE SEAM IS THE HORSES, AND IT IS REACHED BY SUBJECT RATHER THAN BY NAME. *** "Argentine
# Stud Book" returns thirteen genuine articles, and SPORTING LIFE covered Argentine racing in the very
# years GILBERTO LERENA was co-founding that book and having a Palermo Group 1 named for him in 1914.
# *** A targeted read of Sporting Life's Argentine racing columns, 1905-1920, is the thing to do *** -
# and it is a reading task, not a search task.
# *** AND THE TAYLORS WERE SIMPLY NOT NEWSWORTHY. *** A cab driver's household of ten children at
# Northam appears in the press when a daughter passes an examination - which is exactly the one hit this
# archive already holds, the Western Times of 4 April 1901. That is the shape of it, and there is no
# reason to expect much more.
